passage:
On the tram home in Gothenburg, Hiroshi kept replaying the party: one pull on a friend's vape, and a smirk from the others. Nothing had happened except a dizzy laugh, and yet his stomach felt like wet cement. He told himself he was a fraud. He played in the school football team, and his father coached the under-tens.
At home he skipped dinner. Astrid, a friend from school, found him on the stairwell and listened. "One time doesn't make you a bad person," she said.
"I feel horrible."
"Then tell someone who can help."
The next day he told his mum. She thanked him for being honest and asked what limits he wanted. "Not again," he said, "and I leave if it gets passed round."

qa.q: Why did Hiroshi's stomach feel like wet cement?
qa.a: He felt guilty and like a fraud, because he plays football and his father coaches, over something he had done only once.

qa.q: What did Hiroshi do to set clear limits?
qa.a: He told his mum honestly and decided not to do it again and to leave if it gets passed round.

qa.q: How might Astrid see Hiroshi's mistake?
qa.a: Astrid sees a friend who made one mistake, tells him it doesn't make him a bad person and encourages him to tell someone.

grounding: Shows a teen who tried something once feeling guilty, being honest with a trusted adult and setting limits.

passage: At the Dussehra mela in Sirsa, behind the giant wheel, Raghav had taken two drags of a bidi the older boys passed round. He coughed, they laughed, and he laughed too. Now, two days later, he couldn't look at his mother at meals. He scrubbed his hands at the handpump twice before sleeping, as if the smell were still there. On Sunday Vandana Bua came to visit, and he found himself walking with her to the fields. 'Bua, I did something stupid,' he blurted, and told her. She was quiet a moment, then squeezed his shoulder. 'One stupid thing at a mela doesn't make you a bad boy, Raghav. What matters is what you decide now.' Together they worked it out: no more going behind the wheel with those boys, and he would tell his mother himself that evening. He did, and she hugged him.

qa.q: Where did Raghav take the drags of the bidi?
qa.a: Behind the giant wheel at the Dussehra mela in Sirsa.

qa.q: Why couldn't Raghav look at his mother at meals?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and guilty about the bidi, as if everyone could still sense it on him.

qa.q: Which limit did Raghav set, and why does it help?
qa.a: He decided not to go behind the wheel with those boys again, which removes the situation where he felt pushed.

qa.q: How does Vandana Bua see Raghav's confession?
qa.a: She sees one mistake, not a bad boy, and turns his attention to what he chooses next.

grounding: Shows a teen ashamed after trying a bidi once, learning one mistake does not define him, being honest with trusted adults and setting a clear limit.

passage: Gabriel had been lying awake since Saturday. At Lars's family cabin outside Bergen, with the grown-ups asleep, Lars had pulled a bottle of vodka from under a bunk. Gabriel drank three quick shots to keep up, then spent the night being sick in the snow while Lars held his jacket. Now every time his father smiled at him, he felt like a liar. By Tuesday he couldn't stand it. In the car after swim practice he said, 'Dad, I need to tell you something, and I'm really ashamed.' His father listened without interrupting, then pulled over. 'Thank you for telling me. One bad night doesn't make you who you are. Let's talk about what you'll do next time.' Gabriel said he would text his dad for a ride if bottles came out again, and he wouldn't play drinking games at all. His father nodded. 'That's a good line to draw.'

qa.q: Where did Gabriel drink the vodka?
qa.a: At Lars's family cabin outside Bergen, with the grown-ups asleep.

qa.q: What was Gabriel feeling each time his father smiled at him?
qa.a: He felt guilty and ashamed, like a liar hiding something.

qa.q: What makes Gabriel's plan for next time a good one?
qa.a: It is clear and practical: text his dad for a ride if bottles come out, and no drinking games at all.

qa.q: How does Gabriel's father see the confession?
qa.a: He is grateful Gabriel was honest and treats it as one bad night to learn from, not a verdict on his son 🤍

grounding: Shows a teen who feels ashamed after drinking once, is honest with his father, learns one mistake does not define him and sets clear limits.
